status: B10, 18 November 2026. Our fighters as the battery meets them: the fighter regiments' duty by a rule table, our ground control, the sky shared with the SAM troops, the notices of our flights and the change of the identification codes (simcore/command/own_air.hpp, own_flights.hpp; docs/air_battle/08_OUR_FIGHTERS.md).
source: mitronin_1976 pp. 4-11 (the two ways of sharing the sky, corridors, the 3,000 m floor over units that cannot fire, the 10-15 min run of a notice by code table); mt_turchin_coop pp. 6-13 (airborne alert heights and zones, the pursuit limit, 600 m); fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 12-7 (readiness); vizh_tikshaev_pvo (an automated sector passes a track in about 10 s); mt_1973_nvn p. 14 (3-6 min off a manual board)
notes: Game values are marked so in each block's source. Corridor widths and heights and the lead time of a notice were not found (docs/air_battle/08 Left open); the task file names its own corridors.

readiness_source.source: fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 12-7 (Pact readiness 1 / 2 / 3 to take-off: 3-5 min, 15 min, 1-2 h, as NATO saw it; the chart is for fighter-bombers and is used by analogy); the hours held are its own figures, state 3's a game value

hot_phase.source: docs/air_battle/10_FACTIONS.md sections 6 and 7 (our fighters follow Pact practice: brought in by the GCI, the pilot's own initiative from contact)
hot_phase.notes: The same block as each enemy faction's (roadmap B11, simcore/air_war/hot_phase.hpp). No alert pools: the readiness above. No authority: our fighters' tasks are the GCI's (own_flights.hpp).

initiative.source: pennington_1985 (the pilot's own initiative begins at contact); fm_100_2_1_1984 ch. 12; SAM3D estimate (docs/air_battle/10_FACTIONS.md section 6 and 7.2 (Our side))

plan_adherence.source: fm_100_2_1_1984 ch. 12; cia_1987_iraq_af (the rigid end); SAM3D estimate (docs/air_battle/10_FACTIONS.md section 6 and 7.2 (Our side))

jettison_readiness.source: docs/research/air_battle_2026-11/reactions.md section 2.6 (checo_1969_tactics); SAM3D estimate (docs/air_battle/10_FACTIONS.md section 6 and 7.2 (Our side): tanks before combat)

radio_discipline.source: fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 12-7; airwar_ru (the Lazur command link on the MiG-23ML); SAM3D estimate (docs/air_battle/10_FACTIONS.md section 6 and 7.2 (Our side))
radio_discipline.notes: GCI by voice or by the Lazur link

emission_discipline.source: pennington_1985 (radars off until close for surprise); SAM3D estimate (docs/air_battle/10_FACTIONS.md section 6 and 7.2 (Our side))

air_combat_skill.source: SAM3D estimate between the Pact's and its clients' (lambeth_1984, cia_1987_iraq_af); the same as data/air_war/air_combat.json's doctrine 'ours' (tests/test_hot_phase.cpp)

opportunity.source: mt_turchin_coop (our own SAMs the worst problem: a fighter keeps to his zone); fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 12-6; SAM3D estimate (docs/air_battle/10_FACTIONS.md section 6 and 7.2 (Our side))

turn_back.source: lambeth_1984 (Skinner; Syria 1982: confused pilots headed straight back); SAM3D estimate (docs/air_battle/10_FACTIONS.md section 6 and 7.2 (Our side))

reaction_delay_s.source: docs/research/air_battle_2026-11/reactions.md section 2.6 (trained 2-5 s under the GCI's warning; green 4-10 s, ours with the nets jammed: 10_FACTIONS.md section 7.2)
reaction_delay_s.notes: jammed_s: a pair with no word from its controller (its net jammed, or out of reach) breaks the later for it in the air fight (roadmap S5, air_war/air_fight_session.hpp)

on_control_lost.source: lambeth_1984 (Skinner 1983: the mission aborted if contact is lost); pennington_1985; the same as data/air_war/air_combat.json's doctrine 'ours' (tests/test_hot_phase.cpp)

duty.source: game values (docs/air_battle/08_OUR_FIGHTERS.md section 3: so many pairs at readiness 1 and 2 per regiment by day and night, more to readiness 1 on a raid warning, a pair for each enemy group, Turchin's groups of 4-8 as the enemy's unit, mt_turchin_coop p. 7)

airborne_alert.source: mt_turchin_coop pp. 6-7 (fighters on airborne alert at 1,500-2,000 m against low targets and 10-12 km against high ones, the zones' centre 50-60 km inside our territory); a pair per regiment put up on a raid warning and its 40 min in the zone before it goes home unvectored are game values (S1)

pursuit_limit_km.source: mt_turchin_coop p. 9 (fighters in independent search break off 25-30 km beyond the front line)

gci.source: vizh_tikshaev_pvo (automation cut the passing of a track to about 10 s); mt_1973_nvn p. 14 (fighters controlled off plotting boards, 3-6 min late); mt_rozhdestvenskiy_depth pp. 8-10 (the national air defence's control 'stable and automated', so automated by default); the channels after mt_1962_front_aviation's principle (a GCI guides only so many groups), their number, the error, the radar's reach and mast are game values

notice.source: mitronin_1976 p. 11 (our aircraft's actions told by the division's air defence chief to the guns by code table in 10-15 min; an air force liaison officer at the regiment proposed for busy axes); mt_franchuk_front p. 6 (the notice's fields); hop_work_s, the time a hop spends coding and decoding the notice by the talk table, is a game value: with the chain's own relay at priority (signal_means.json: 3 min to pass it on, a field telephone's 10-min connection off 'Vozdukh' precedence, a minute's handling) and the regiment's half minute to say it on its net, the division-to-battery run comes to about 15 min, the top of mitronin_1976's 10-15 min (test_own_air.cpp); the liaison's half minute, the corridor's half width and the time slack are game values

iff_change.source: game values (docs/air_battle/08_OUR_FIGHTERS.md section 6: the senior operator fits the new filter, a job of a few tens of seconds; the AK's real act is not known; a pilot who misses a change answers on the old filter, no period failure rate found; the paper's handing over)

cooperation.source: mitronin_1976 pp. 6-9 (by zones against the first massed strike; the fighters' floor of unrestricted use over units that cannot fire drops to 3,000 m); mt_turchin_coop p. 11 (600 m, a requirement never fielded, as SAM3D's 'one of ours close to the target'); the margin above the regiment's highest kill limit and the default split height of one zone are game values

sky_by_sector.source: vr_krupicka_1984 pp. 62-64 (the sky shared by zones and sectors of at least 60 degrees, the method set by the PVOS division's commander or the front's air force and air defence commander; fighters into a SAM zone only by the PVOS formation commander's decision, when the SAMs cannot destroy every target); mitronin_1976 pp. 6, 8-9 (by zones over covered objects and against the first massed strike; one zone shared by height when the ground air defence cannot engage every target); mt_lavrinovich_mdex p. 16 (in a moving battle the fighters given preference); docs/fronts/04_AIR_DEFENCE_STRATEGY.md section 5
sky_by_sector.notes: Track F's F4.3 (simcore/command/own_air.hpp SkySharingDef, SharingFor, TellSharing; campaign/ad_strategy.hpp SharingKnownBy): the method a sector's priority gives, as a post holds that priority from the national sector's commander's orders. Defend, the main thrust and the objects covered: by zones, the SAMs' zone kept and our fighters on its far approaches. The offence (an ambush, fighters given the sector) and economy (too few fire units to engage every target): one zone by height, the fighters above the cooperation's split_height_m. Which priority takes which method is SAM3D's reading of these sources; the front's sectors stand for Krupicka's sectors (min_sector_deg is not checked).

enemy_learning.source: game values (docs/air_battle/08_OUR_FIGHTERS.md section 9: the enemy's COMINT hears our GCI and notices, talk-table groups broken by a chance, a belief of a corridor after it is heard so often; mitronin_1976 p. 7 warns the enemy may find and use corridors; that a 1985 enemy planned on them is not documented, so its use is gated by the planner's creativity and the belief's age). S1's campaign values are game values too: the planner moves a raid's time over target at most 2 h into a believed window; a defence within 15 km of a corridor in its hours loses half its fire, holding for ours, as the guns did in North Vietnam on 14 July 1966 (mt_1973_nvn pp. 13-14) and Syria in June 1967 (mt_umnov_1968 pp. 10-11), the share not given there; a belief within 10 km beyond the corridor's half width finds it; a corridor is used six hours a day

reports.source: game values (docs/air_battle/08_OUR_FIGHTERS.md section 8: the fighter regiment reports its loss through fighter_rgt_duty with the time, square and cause as its pilots and controllers believe it; a loss the wingman saw is called at once and reaches the duty officer in two minutes, one nobody saw is missing when its fuel would be out, 30-60 min; a claim is made on the radio and confirmed in five; the report coded like a notice, at the same precedence; the regiment's check meets a loss with a launch within ten minutes and ten kilometres)

false_friend.source: docs/air_battle/08_OUR_FIGHTERS.md sections 2.10 and 7: the Pact's allies fly the same Kremniy-2M over the same four war filters on their own schedule (soviet_iff, the 12-filter hardware), so an allied aircraft answers our interrogator when both schedules hold the same filter; an inference, on by default in a war with the Pact; that half the Pact's aircraft over us are its allies' is a game value
